import os
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import lightgbm as lgb
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
from sklearn.metrics import log_loss

# Ensure submission directory exists
os.makedirs("./submission", exist_ok=True)

# Load data
input_dir = "./input"
train_df = pd.read_csv(f"{input_dir}/train.csv")
test_df = pd.read_csv(f"{input_dir}/test.csv")
sample_submission = pd.read_csv(f"{input_dir}/sample_submission.csv")

print(f"Train shape: {train_df.shape}")
print(f"Test shape: {test_df.shape}")
print(f"Sample submission shape: {sample_submission.shape}")

# Identify features and labels
feature_cols = [col for col in train_df.columns if col not in ["id", "species"]]
id_col = "id"
target_col = "species"

# Prepare train and test features and labels
X_train = train_df[feature_cols].values
y_train = train_df[target_col].values
X_test = test_df[feature_cols].values
test_ids = test_df[id_col].values

# Get the order of species from sample_submission (this defines column order for submission)
species_cols = list(sample_submission.columns[1:])
print(f"Number of species columns: {len(species_cols)}")

# Get unique classes from training data
unique_classes = np.unique(y_train)
print(f"Unique classes in training: {len(unique_classes)}")

# Use stratified 80/20 split for validation
X_tr, X_val, y_tr, y_val = train_test_split(
    X_train, y_train, test_size=0.2, random_state=42, stratify=y_train
)

print(f"Train split: {X_tr.shape}, Validation split: {X_val.shape}")

# Simplified LightGBM with faster training parameters
model = lgb.LGBMClassifier(
    n_estimators=25,
    max_depth=6,
    num_leaves=24,
    learning_rate=0.2,
    min_child_samples=50,
    subsample=0.9,
    colsample_bytree=0.9,
    random_state=42,
    verbose=-1,
    n_jobs=-1,
    early_stopping_rounds=100,  # Set high to avoid early stopping interruption
    verbose_eval=False,
)

# Train on training split only - never sees validation data
print("Training model...")
model.fit(X_tr, y_tr, eval_set=[(X_val, y_val)])

print(f"Model stopped after {model.n_estimators_} estimators")

# Get validation predictions (model never trained on this set)
y_val_pred_raw = model.predict_proba(X_val)

# Calculate multi-class log loss on hold-out validation set
y_val_pred_clipped = np.clip(y_val_pred_raw, 1e-15, 1 - 1e-15)
val_logloss = log_loss(y_val, y_val_pred_clipped, labels=unique_classes)
print(f"Validation log loss (hold-out): {val_logloss:.6f}")

# Get test predictions
y_test_pred_raw = model.predict_proba(X_test)

# Apply clipping to ensure probabilities are in valid range [1e-15, 1-1e-15]
y_test_pred = np.clip(y_test_pred_raw, 1e-15, 1 - 1e-15)

# Create submission DataFrame matching sample_submission format exactly
# Order: id column first, then species columns in order from sample_submission
submission_df = pd.DataFrame(0, index=test_ids, columns=["id"] + species_cols)

# Fill in species predictions (in correct column order)
for i, species_col in enumerate(species_cols):
    submission_df[species_col] = y_test_pred[:, i]

# Set ID column
submission_df["id"] = test_ids.astype(str)

# Ensure correct column order
submission_df = submission_df[["id"] + species_cols]

print(f"Submission shape: {submission_df.shape}")
print(f"Submission columns: {list(submission_df.columns)}")
print(f"Submission IDs: {submission_df['id'].nunique()} unique")

# Save submission
submission_df.to_csv("./submission/submission.csv", index=False)
print("Submission saved to ./submission/submission.csv")

# Verify submission
sample = submission_df.head()
print(f"Sample submission shape: {sample.shape}")
print(f"Sample columns: {list(submission_df.columns)}")

print(f"\nHold-out validation log loss: {val_logloss:.6f}")

SUBMISSION PREDICTION REVIEW (ADVISORY)
Training labels y_train are passed to LGBMClassifier.fit(), which internally maps classes to indices via np.unique(y_train) (first-occurrence order). predict_proba returns probabilities in that internal order. Submission columns are taken from sample_submission.columns[1:], which are alphabetically ordered species names. y_test_pred[:, i] is assigned to species_cols[i] without remapping, so column i receives probability for model.classes_[i], not species_cols[i].
